'''Jeremy John Gray''' (born 25 April 1947) is an English [[mathematician]] primarily interested in the history of mathematics.

==Biography==
Gray studied mathematics at the [[University of Oxford]] from 1966 to 1969, and then at [[Warwick University]], obtaining his PhD in 1980 under the supervision of [[Ian Stewart (mathematician)|Ian Stewart]] and [[David Fowler (mathematician)|David Fowler]]. He has worked at the [[Open University]] since 1974, and became a lecturer there in 1978. He also lectured at the [[University of Warwick]] from 2002 to 2017, teaching a course on the history of mathematics.

Gray was a consultant on the [[television]] series, ''[[The Story of Maths]]'',<ref name = Ep4>''To Infinity and Beyond'' 27 October 2008 21:00 BBC Four</ref> a co-production between the [[Open University]] and the [[BBC]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Science Weekly podcast: The story of maths |date=2008-10-13 |website=[[The Guardian]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221028151519/https://www.theguardian.com/science/blog/audio/2008/oct/13/science-weekly-podcast |archive-date=2022-10-28 |url-status=live |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/blog/audio/2008/oct/13/science-weekly-podcast}}</ref> He edits [[Archive for History of Exact Sciences]].

In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Gray, Jeremy J.|chapter=The Riemann-Roch theorem and geometry, 1854–1914|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=811–822|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011634000}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref>

== Books ==

Gray has been awarded prizes for his contributions to mathematics, including the [[Albert Leon Whiteman Memorial Prize]] from the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2009,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/maths/general/news/2009/#jgray|title = Warwick Mathematics Institute News 2009}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=January 2009 Prizes and Awards | url=https://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/prizebooklet-2009.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209012111/http://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/prizebooklet-2009.pdf | archive-date=2021-02-09}}</ref> the Otto Neugebauer Prize of the [[European Mathematical Society]] in 2016,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.7ecm.de/prizes/laureates.html|title = 7ECM – Laureates}}</ref> and the [[London Mathematical Society]]'s [[Hirst Prize and Lectureship]] in 2018.

He has authored the following:

* ''Ideas of space: Euclidean, non-Euclidean, and relativistic''. Oxford University Press 1979, 2nd edition 1989, Spanish edition, Ideas de Espacio, Mondadori Espana, 1992. Romanian edition, Idei Spatiu, Editura All Educational, 1998.
* ''Linear differential equations and group theory from Riemann to Poincaré'' Birkhäuser, 1986, 2nd edition with three new appendices and other additional material, 2000, Japanese edition 2002.
* ''The Geometrical Work of Girard Desargues'' (with [[Judith V. Field|J. V. Field]]). Springer 1986. {{cite book|title=2012 pbk edition|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zSvSBwAAQBAJ|isbn=978-1-4613-8694-0 | last1=Field | first1=Judith V. | last2=Gray | first2=Jeremy | date=6 December 2012 | publisher=Springer }}
* ''Geometry'' (with D.A. Brannan and M. Esplen). Cambridge University Press 1999, 2nd edition 2012, Arabic edition 2001.
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=z-mh6YwRIWIC ''The Hilbert Challenge'']. Oxford University Press 2000,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Blank, Brian E.|author-link=Brian Blank|title=joint review of ''The Hilbert Challenge'' by Jeremy Gray and ''The Honors Class'' by Benjamin Yandell|date=September 2002|pages=911–915|volume=49|issue=8|journal=Notices of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200208/rev-blank.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Graves, David|date=January 18, 2001|title=Review of ''The Hilbert Challenge'' by Jeremy Gray|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-hilbert-challenge|access-date=9 October 2023|archive-date=4 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204102247/https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-hilbert-challenge|url-status=dead}}</ref> French translation Le défi de Hilbert Dunod, 2003, Taiwanese translation 2003, Spanish translation El reto de Hilbert Critica, 2004. 
* ''János Bolyai, non-Euclidean Geometry and the Nature of Space''. Burndy Library, MIT, 2004.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Osserman, Robert|author-link=Robert Osserman|date=October 2005|volume=52|issue=9|title=review of '' János Bolyai, Non-Euclidean Geometry, and the Nature of Space'' by Jeremy Gray|pages=1030–1034|journal=Notices of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200509/rev-osserman.pdf}}</ref> 
* ''Worlds out of Nothing; A Course on the History of Geometry in the 19th Century''. Springer 2006, 2nd revised edition 2010.
* ''Plato’s Ghost: The Modernist Transformation of Mathematics''. Princeton University Press 2008.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Rowe, David E.|authorlink=David E. Rowe|title=Review: ''Plato's ghost: the modernist transformation of mathematics'' by Jeremy Gray|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=2012|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-2012-01403-9|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Wilders, Richard J.|title=review of ''Plato's Ghost: The Modernist Transformation of Mathematics'' by Jeremy Gray|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|date=June 8, 2009|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/platos-ghost-the-modernist-transformation-of-mathematics|access-date=14 May 2024|archive-date=14 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240514061228/https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/platos-ghost-the-modernist-transformation-of-mathematics|url-status=dead}}</ref> {{isbn|9780691136103}}
* [https://archive.org/details/henripoincaresci0000gray ''Henri Poincaré: a scientific biography'']. Princeton University Press 2012.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Stillwell, John|author-link=John Stillwell|title=Review of ''Henri Poincaré. A Scientific Biography'' by Jeremy Gray|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=61|issue=4|year=2014|pages=378–383|url=https://community.ams.org/notices/201404/rnoti-p378.pdf}}</ref>
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=X08dgn3YcLwC ''Hidden Harmony – Geometric Fantasies. The Rise of Complex Function Theory''] (with [[Umberto Bottazzini]]). Springer 2013.<ref>{{cite web|author=Das, Tushar|title=Review of ''Hidden Harmony – Geometric Fantasies. The Rise of Complex Function Theory'' by Umberto Bottazzini and Jeremy Gray|date=July 29, 2015|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/hidden-harmony-geometric-fantasies-the-rise-of-complex-function-theory|access-date=9 October 2023|archive-date=5 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205214137/https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/hidden-harmony-geometric-fantasies-the-rise-of-complex-function-theory|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* ''The Real and the Complex: A History of Analysis in the 19th Century''. Springer 2015.
* ''A History of Abstract Algebra: From Algebraic Equations to Modern Algebra''. Springer 2018.
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=oKkxEAAAQBAJ ''Change and Variations: A History of Differential Equations to 1900'']. Springer 2021.

Books edited or co-edited:
* ''The History of Mathematics; a Reader'' (with [[John Fauvel]]). Macmillan 1987. 
* ''L'Europe mathématique, Mathematical Europe'' (with [[Catherine Goldstein|C. Goldstein]] and J. Ritter). Edited with an introductory essay, Éditions de la maison des sciences de l'homme, Paris 1996.
* ''Henri Poincaré: Three Supplementary Essays on the Discovery of Fuchsian Functions'' (with Scott Walter) Edited with an introductory essay, Akademie Verlag and Blanchard 1997.
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=VbSATwMDFg8C ''The symbolic universe: geometry and physics, 1890-1930'']. Edited with an introduction and an essay, Oxford University Press 1999.
* ''Jacques Hadamard: Non-Euclidean Geometry in the Theory of Automorphic Functions'' (with Abe Shenitzer), translated Abe Shenitzer with an introductory essay by J.J. Gray, American and London Mathematical Societies Series in the History of Mathematics, HMath17, 1999.
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=e0TTBwAAQBAJ ''Mathematical Conversations; Selections from the Mathematical Intelligencer''] (with [[Robin Wilson (mathematician)|Robin Wilson]]) Springer 2000. There is also a Japanese edition.
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=4mwSrfxBSzkC ''Gauss − Titan of Science'']. A re-edition of [[G. Waldo Dunnington]]'s book of 1956, with a new introduction and appendices by J.J. Gray, Mathematical Association of America, 2003.
* The Architecture of Modern Mathematics. Edited volume, with an essay by J.J. Gray and one with the co-editor, José Ferreirós, Oxford University Press 2006.
* ''Episodes in the History of Modern Algebra 1800—1950''. Edited volume, with an introduction by J.J. Gray and the co-editor, [[Karen Parshall]], American and London Mathematical Societies Series in the History of Mathematics, HMath32, 2007.

He has also contributed to other books:
* ''[[The Princeton Companion to Mathematics]]''
* ''The Oxford Handbook of the History of Mathematics''
* ''[[Revolutions in Mathematics]]''
